issues.description: Logic error in quat-from-euler: the 'y' component calculation uses '(* sr sp sy)' which is a typo for '(* sr cp sy)'. This results in incorrect quaternion values for ZYX Euler rotations.
The quat-slerp function performs two redundant calls to quat-dot for the same pair of quaternions, which is inefficient for a performance-critical interpolation routine.
Hardcoded PI literal (3.141592653589793) used in quat-to-euler instead of a global constant, which is inconsistent with Core library standards.

files_reviewed.notes: The implementation is mathematically sound for most operations, but the Euler conversion bug will cause subtle rotation errors in 3D pipelines.

issues.description: Deflation logic in qr-algorithm-shifted-loop is flawed. It reduces the 'active-size' for shift calculation but continues to perform QR decomposition on the full-sized matrix. This negates the performance benefits of deflation and can introduce numerical noise into already converged eigenvalues.
The eigen-decomposition function uses unit vectors as a fallback when inverse iteration fails to converge. This is mathematically incorrect as unit vectors are not eigenvectors of general matrices.
wilkinson-shift lacks a guard for the case where d=0 and discriminant < 0 for non-symmetric matrices, potentially leading to a division by zero if tolerance is very small.

files_reviewed.notes: The QR algorithm needs to be updated to work on sub-matrices during deflation to be competitive and stable.

issues.description: d-pow implementation lacks handling for negative exponents (n < 0), which will result in infinite recursion and a stack overflow.
derivative-at relies on hardcoded list indexing (cadr) of the resolution result. This is brittle and will fail if the instance database order changes or if resolution returns a decorated result.

files_reviewed.notes: Elegant use of the type-class pattern for AD, but generic numeric utilities like d-pow must handle the full range of integer inputs.

issues.description: normalize-signal does not check for empty vectors, leading to a division by zero error when calculating the mean for a signal of length zero.

find-peaks uses non-strict inequalities (>=) for neighbor comparisons. In the presence of a plateau in the signal, it will return multiple indices for the same peak instead of a single peak or the plateau center.

files_reviewed.notes: Strong FFT-based convolution implementation. Added robustness against empty inputs is required for Core stability.

summary: While the codebase demonstrates sophisticated mathematical implementations, there are critical logic errors in coordinate transformations and algorithm efficiency. Specifically, the quaternion Euler conversion typo and the inefficient QR deflation are high-priority fixes. Additionally, several functions require better guard clauses for edge cases like empty signals or negative parameters.
